minutes.headline: Select Board approved the 30 School Street demolition bid package, telework policy and appointment policy; ARPA policy only presented.
minutes.summary: The board heard from the new state representative and the library director, appointed an associate member to the Green Communities Committee, and approved the invitation for bids for hazardous material abatement and demolition at 30 School Street. It approved the remote work policy, the appointments policy and the volunteer application forms. The town manager presented a draft ARPA/CLFRF distribution policy with proposed allocations, which drew initial reactions and will be revised; members split on keeping fully remote meetings under the open meeting law.

public_comment.topic: Incoming state representative introduced herself, thanked the board and said she would meet with the town manager on priorities.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to approve the invitation for bids for hazardous material abatement and demolition at 30 School Street.
The board unanimously approved the telework policy as presented and the appointment policy as amended.
The board approved new volunteer appointment and reappointment application forms, with a typo correction.
The town manager presented a draft ARPA/CLFRF distribution policy with proposed allocations; it was discussed but not voted, and will be revised.
Members split on keeping fully remote meetings under the open meeting law; the question returns on a future agenda.

why_it_matters: The bid package moves the 30 School Street demolition toward contractor pricing, and the draft ARPA policy works as a spending plan for federal pandemic-relief money that must be obligated by the end of 2024 and spent by the end of 2026.
The remote-meeting question decides whether residents can attend or comment on board meetings from home, and no position has been settled.
watch_next: January 10 meeting: revised ARPA/CLFRF distribution policy, after members send feedback to the town manager by about January 4.
A future agenda item on the open meeting law remote-meeting position.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the five non-procedural votes (all passed), the warrants, the $350,000/$60,000 demolition estimate and the January 4 ARPA feedback deadline. They differ on the follow-up date for the Open Meeting Law discussion and on the names of several people, and the official minutes do not record the ARPA award total or the burial cost estimate.
